title: Mindful Eating: A Path to Healthy Body
seo_title: Mindful Eating Class 6 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 3)
standard_text: Food and its components: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, dietary fibre and water; testing foods for starch, protein and fat; deficiency diseases; balanced diet, millets and regional food habits; mindful eating (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 3).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 6 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 3: nutrients and their sources, food tests for starch, protein and fat, deficiency diseases, millets and a balanced diet. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A balanced diet has all the nutrients.
body_html:
How to think about it

Our food contains nutrients: carbohydrates and fats give energy, proteins build and repair the body, and vitamins and minerals keep us healthy. Dietary fibre and water do not give energy, but we need them too. A balanced diet has all of these in the right amounts.

We can test foods: iodine solution turns starch blue-black, copper sulphate with sodium hydroxide turns protein violet, and fat leaves an oily patch on paper. A long lack of a nutrient causes a deficiency disease, such as scurvy (vitamin C) or anaemia (iron).

Example

A potato slice turns blue-black with iodine. Which nutrient?

iodine tests for starch

Answer: starch (a carbohydrate)

Example

Bleeding gums: which vitamin is lacking?

scurvy

Answer: vitamin C

Common mistakes

  • Thinking fibre gives energy.
  • Mixing up the tests for starch and protein.
  • Saying rickets is caused by a lack of vitamin C.

faq.q: Why are millets good for us?
faq.a: They are rich in fibre, minerals such as calcium and iron, and vitamins, and they grow with little water.
